chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: If a man is on a journey and the time for salat enters before he reaches his family, then he continues traveling until he enters upon his family, then if he wishes he may shorten, and if he wishes he may complete; and if he completes, that is more beloved to me.

key_terms.أَتَمَّ: performed the prayer in full, complete form
key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his family or home, indicating return to residence
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel or journey that affects the ruling of salat
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: performed the prayer in shortened form as a traveler
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: the legally designated time for performing the prayer

ai.seo_question: If prayer time starts while traveling but I reach home before praying, should I shorten or complete the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a traveler for whom the time of salat begins before arriving home, but who delays the prayer until reaching his family. Upon arrival, he is given a choice between shortened and complete prayer, though completing it is stated to be preferable.
